mainTopic: What it means that תכלת and לבן do not hold each other back: the order of the strings, cut-short strings and their minimum length, and tying a knot after each set of windings
overview: This amud explains the משנה's rule that the white (לבן) and sky-blue (תכלת) strings of ציצית do not hold each other back. The גמרא first rejects reading 'he lacked a מצוה' as leaving out the white strings, because according to רבי the two kinds depend on each other. Instead, רב says it means he did the מצוה, just not in the best way. רמי בר חמא, backed up by a talk between לוי and שמואל, explains that the strings matching the garment's color should go first: white on a linen garment, תכלת on an all-תכלת garment. Getting the order wrong is still valid after the fact. רבא rejects the idea that color decides anything and says the rule is about strings that were cut short. The sons of רבי חייא support this: cut-short strings are kosher if enough is left to tie a loop. Whether that means tying all the strings together or each one alone stays a תיקו, and thick strings are kosher all the more. Finally, the גמרא names רבי יוחנן בן נורי as the תנא who disagrees with רבי. רבא then proves that a knot must be tied after each set of windings.

steps.title: It cannot mean he skipped the white strings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests one possible meaning of 'he lacked a מצוה': that he skipped the white strings and kept only the תכלת. It rejects this, because according to רבי each kind of string holds back the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means he left out the מצוה of white strings and only did the מצוה of תכלת, that cannot be right. According to רבי, the two hold each other back, so he would not have fulfilled anything at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to understand what 'he lacked a מצוה' means. It tests the most obvious reading and shows that it fails according to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that one part of the מצוה, the white, was missing, while the other part, the תכלת, was done. But רבי holds that לבן and תכלת are each necessary for the other. So if the white was missing, the תכלת would not count either. That means this reading cannot be what 'he lacked a מצוה' means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא tests a possible reading)
He lacked or was missing a מצוה
The white strings of ציצית
The sky-blue strings of ציצית
They hold each other back: without one, the other does not count

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה's rule that לבן and תכלת do NOT hold each other back. Here the גמרא is pointing out that according to רבי they DO, so 'lacked a מצוה' cannot mean that one kind of string was missing.

phrases.english: If you say he omitted the מצוה of white
and fulfilled the מצוה of sky-blue —
according to Rabbi, they prevent each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא חִיסֵּר מִצְוָה דְּלָבָן וְקִיֵּים מִצְוָה דִּתְכֵלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the phrase 'he lacked a מצוה'
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'he lacked a מצוה' means the white strings were left out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי, לבן and תכלת each hold back the other, so leaving out the white would cancel the whole מצוה, not just part of it.

steps.title: Lacking a מצוה means not doing it in the best way
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that he fulfilled the מצוה but missed doing it in the most ideal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means he lacked a מצוה but still did the מצוה. What does 'lacked a מצוה' mean? That he did not do the מצוה in the best possible way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting רב, gives the correct meaning: the person did fulfill ציצית, just not in the best way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing was actually missing from the ציצית. Only the ideal order, white first, was not followed. That is why the מצוה still counts, even according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did fulfill the מצוה
Doing a מצוה in the best, most ideal way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows an important general idea: a person can fulfill a מצוה at the basic level and still fall short of the ideal way of doing it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
that he omitted a מצוה and performed a מצוה,
and what is 'omitted a מצוה'?
That he did not perform the מצוה in the optimal manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֶׁחִיסֵּר מִצְוָה וְעָשָׂה מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He lacked a מצוה' means a whole part of the מצוה was missing
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only that the ideal way of doing the מצוה, the right order, was not kept

steps.title: What does 'תכלת does not hold back לבן' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The order-based reading works for 'לבן does not hold back תכלת', but the other half of the rule seems to have no meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for 'the white does not hold back the תכלת'. But 'the תכלת does not hold back the white', what does that mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on the order-based explanation. It fits one half of the rule but not the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the white strings should go in first. So 'לבן does not hold back תכלת' means that if you put the תכלת in first, it still counts. But since the תכלת is not supposed to come first anyway, what case would 'תכלת does not hold back לבן' be talking about?

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (the setup before a question)
What is it? What could it mean?

phrases.english: This works out well for white
that it does not prevent the sky-blue,
sky-blue that does not prevent the white —
what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח לָבָן דְּאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַתְּכֵלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order-based reading accepted in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the rule 'they do not hold each other back' as being about the order of the strings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: White normally comes first, so a rule that the תכלת does not hold back the white seems to describe no real case.

steps.title: A garment made entirely of תכלת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the second half of the rule is about a garment made entirely of תכלת, where the תכלת strings should go first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: it is needed only for a garment that is entirely תכלת.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the question by finding a case where the תכלת normally comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a garment made entirely of תכלת, the תכלת strings are supposed to go in first. So the rule teaches that if you put the white in first there, it still counts. Now both halves of the rule have a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this case)
A garment made entirely of sky-blue wool

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the rule are about order. Usually white comes first, but in a garment made entirely of תכלת, the תכלת comes first. Either way, getting the order wrong does not cancel the מצוה; it only means it was not done in the best way.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
It is necessary only
for a garment that is entirely sky-blue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule 'תכלת does not hold back לבן' describes no real case
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a garment made entirely of תכלת, where the תכלת strings come first

steps.title: Levi asks שמואל to explain the double rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a parallel report that will support the order-based reading. לוי urgently asks שמואל what the משנה's rule about תכלת and לבן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: לוי said to שמואל, 'Great one, don't sit down until you explain this to me: what does it mean that תכלת doesn't hold back the white, and the white doesn't hold back the תכלת?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'this was also stated' and brings a second conversation that will back up the earlier explanation. This step is the setup: לוי asks the question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words איתמר נמי signal support for the answer just given by רמי בר חמא. In this second report, שמואל answers one half of the rule (step 6), and רמי בר חמא answers the other half with the same all-תכלת garment case (step 8). לוי's question is the same puzzle: the משנה's two-sided rule cannot simply mean you may skip one kind, so what does it mean?

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also stated': a separate teaching that agrees with what was just said
A title of honor for שמואל, like 'great one' or 'master'
Holds back: one thing stops the מצוה from counting without the other
The sky-blue string of ציצית
The white strings of ציצית

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new discussion. The גמרא is bringing a second source that says the same thing as steps 2–4, to show that the idea is backed up.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Levi said to Shmuel: Aryokh,
phrases.notes: אריוך is a nickname of honor for שמואל, something like 'great one'.

phrases.english: do not sit down on your feet
until you explain this matter to me:
the sky-blue does not hold back the white,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַלָּבָן אֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַתְּכֵלֶת – מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: and the white does not hold back the sky-blue – what does it mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לֵוִי לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source that will support the order-based reading of רב and רמי בר חמא from steps 2–4.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's rule is about the order of tying the strings, not about leaving one kind out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A conversation between לוי and שמואל, answered in the next step.

steps.title: שמואל: on a linen garment the white goes first
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the rule is about a linen garment, where the white strings should go first, but תכלת first is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: this is needed only for a linen garment with ציצית, where the מצוה is to put the white strings first. Why? Because 'the corner' in the פסוק means strings of the same kind as the corner. Still, if he put the תכלת before the white, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about which strings go on first. On a white linen garment the white goes first, but doing it the other way still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the fringe of the corner' before it mentions the תכלת. 'The corner' means strings that match the garment, which is white for linen, so those come first. The משנה's words 'white does not hold back תכלת' teach that getting the order wrong does not ruin the ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: A linen sheet or cloak. Linen is usually white
To put first, to do earlier
The same kind as the corner: strings that match the garment's material and color
We have no problem with it. It is valid after the fact

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between the best way to do a מצוה and what still counts. Putting the matching strings first is the ideal, but the other order is still kosher.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is needed only for a linen cloak with ציצית,
where the מצוה is to put the white first.
What is the reason? 'The corner' – strings of the same kind as the corner,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38. 'The corner' comes before 'תכלת' in the פסוק, so the matching strings go first.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַקְדֵּים תְּכֵלֶת לְלָבָן – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: and if he put the sky-blue before the white – we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְסָדִין בְּצִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's question by placing the rule in the case of a linen garment and the order of the strings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On a linen garment the white goes first because of 'הכנף – מין כנף', but תכלת first is still valid.

steps.title: What about the other half of the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: this explains 'white does not hold back תכלת', but what does 'תכלת does not hold back white' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, that explains why the white does not hold back the תכלת. But what does it mean that the תכלת does not hold back the white?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל's answer only covers one half of the משנה's rule. It asks what the other half could mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a linen garment the white is supposed to go first, so the only possible mistake is putting תכלת first. That explains only one half of the rule. The reverse half, about putting white first by mistake, still has no case to describe.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That works out fine': it accepts one part and challenges another
What is it? What case does it describe?

phrases.aramaic: תִּינַח לָבָן דְּאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַתְּכֵלֶת,
phrases.english: It works out well that the white does not hold back the sky-blue,

phrases.aramaic: תְּכֵלֶת דְּאֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת הַלָּבָן מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: but the sky-blue not holding back the white, what does it mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח לָבָן דְּאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַתְּכֵלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer for covering only one half of the משנה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's order-based reading of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If white normally goes first, the half saying 'תכלת does not hold back white' seems to describe no real case.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: a garment made all of תכלת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the other half is about a garment made entirely of תכלת, where the תכלת should go first, but white first is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: it is needed only for a garment made entirely of תכלת. There the מצוה is to put the תכלת first, because 'the corner' means strings that match the garment. Still, if he put the white first, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא finds a case for the second half of the rule: a sky-blue garment, where the ideal order flips. With this, both halves of the משנה make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule, 'הכנף – מין כנף', is used again. The strings that match the garment go first. On a blue garment that means תכלת first, so 'תכלת does not hold back white' teaches that putting white first is still kosher. Both halves are now about order, never about skipping a kind.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment made entirely of sky-blue material
First, at the beginning
'It is needed only for…': it points to the specific case a rule is about

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of 'תכלת and לבן do not hold each other back' are about ORDER. The strings matching the garment go first (white on linen, תכלת on a blue garment). The wrong order is still valid after the fact. The parallel report from לוי and שמואל backs up this reading.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְטַלִּית שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ תְּכֵלֶת,
phrases.english: It is needed only for a garment that is entirely sky-blue,
where the מצוה is to put the sky-blue first,
since 'the corner' means strings of the same kind as the corner,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַקְדֵּים לָבָן בְּרֵישָׁא לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: and if he put the white first, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְטַלִּית שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ תְּכֵלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by finding a case for the second half of the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a specific case (a garment entirely of תכלת) where the ideal order is reversed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second half of the rule seemed to describe no real case.
steps.terutzMaskana: On an all-תכלת garment the תכלת goes first. Putting white first is still valid, so both halves of the rule are about order.

steps.title: רבא asks: does the color really decide the order?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the whole order-based reading of שמואל and רמי בר חמא: why should the color of the garment decide which strings go first?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it the color that decides this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanations we just saw. Those explanations said the color of the garment decides which strings you put in first, and he questions that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said white goes first on a linen (white) garment, and רמי בר חמא said תכלת goes first on an all-תכלת garment. רבא asks why the garment's color should have any say in the order of the strings. With this, the whole order-based reading is thrown into doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really...? (opens a doubting question)
Color, dye
Causes, decides

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is it the color that decides it?
phrases.notes: He means the color of the garment, which the last two answers used to decide which strings go first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי צִיבְעָא קָא גָרֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order-based explanations of שמואל (step 6) and רמי בר חמא (step 8).
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the garment's color decides whether white or תכלת strings go first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The color of the garment seems to have no logical connection to the order of the strings, so the reading looks baseless.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: the rule is about strings cut short
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה differently. If either the תכלת or the white strings are cut short and the others remain, the ציצית are still kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The rule is needed only for cut-short strings. If the תכלת got cut and the white remains, or the white got cut and the תכלת remains, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a completely new explanation of the משנה. It is not about order at all; it is about strings that got cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One does not hold back the other' now means: damage to one color doesn't ruin the ציצית, while the other color remains, and the cut-short strings themselves still count if enough is left to tie. So each color is judged on its own. One kind being cut short does not make the whole thing פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (narrows a rule to one case)
Strings that were cut or worn down to stubs
Was cut short
We have no problem with it; it is fine

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a completely different way to read the משנה's rule: it is not about order at all, but about cut-short strings of one color not making the ציצית פסול.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is needed only for cut-short strings,
that if the sky-blue was cut short and the white remains,
or if the white was cut short and the sky-blue remains,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְגַרְדּוּמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge by replacing the order-based reading with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case of the משנה (from order of insertion to cut-short strings)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about which color of string must be put in first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that if one color is cut short and the other remains, the ציצית are kosher.

steps.title: Support: the sons of רבי חייא say cut strings are kosher
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא teach that cut-short תכלת strings are kosher, and so is a cut-short אזוב. This backs up רבא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the sons of רבי חייא say: cut-short תכלת strings are kosher, and cut-short אזוב is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that supports רבא. Cut-short strings really can still be kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reading only works if cut-short strings can be kosher at all. The sons of רבי חייא say exactly that. They add a parallel case: an אזוב branch that got broken down is also still usable.

keyTerms.meaning: The cut-short remains of
Hyssop, a plant used for sprinkling in purification
Kosher, valid

phrases.english: As the sons of Rabbi Chiya say:
Cut-short sky-blue strings are kosher,
and cut-short hyssop is kosher.
phrases.notes: The אזוב is the bundle used to sprinkle the פרה אדומה water.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source backing up רבא's claim that cut-short strings are kosher.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that cut-short strings of one color don't make the ציצית פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of בני רבי חייא: גרדומי תכלת and גרדומי אזוב are kosher.

steps.title: How long must the cut strings still be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what minimum length cut-short strings need in order to stay kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the measure for cut-short strings?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that cut strings can be kosher, the גמרא asks how short is too short. It is setting up שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cut-short is kosher' can't mean any stub at all. There must be some minimum, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: How much
A set measurement or minimum size

phrases.english: And what is the measure of cut-short strings?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה שִׁיעוּר גַּרְדּוּמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limit of the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum length a cut-short string must keep to stay kosher.

steps.title: שמואל: long enough to tie a loop
steps.stepSummary: בר המדורי reports in the name of שמואל that cut strings must still be long enough to tie into a loop.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר המדורי said in the name of שמואל: enough to tie them in a loop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer. The strings must still be long enough to tie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum isn't a number of fingers or inches. It is a practical test: can you still tie the strings into a loop (עניבה)? If so, they are kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough to
To tie them in a loop or slipknot (עֲנִיבָה)

phrases.english: Bar Hamduri said that Shmuel said:
Enough to tie them in a loop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּדֵי לְעׇנְבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cut-short strings must still be long enough to tie in a loop.

steps.title: All strings tied together, or each one alone?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask what 'enough to tie' means: long enough to tie all the strings together, or just long enough to tie each string by itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: 'Enough to tie them' means to tie all of them together, or maybe each one by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about שמואל's measure. It wants to know which kind of tying counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying all the strings together as a bundle needs more length than tying a single string. So the question is whether the minimum is the bigger amount (all together) or the smaller amount (each alone).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open dilemma)
Together, with each other
Or perhaps
By itself, alone

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
'Enough to tie them in a loop' –
does it mean to tie all of them together,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֹּל חַד וְחַד לְחוֹדֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps each one by itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: כְּדֵי לְעׇנְבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand שמואל's measure from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'enough to tie' means tying all the strings together or each string alone.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: it remains unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the last question and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. Whether the length needed is 'all together' or 'each alone' stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question was silly or rejected. It means it is a real question that the גמרא could not settle.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 14 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains undecided whether 'enough to tie' means all the strings together or each one alone.

steps.title: Thick strings too stiff to tie
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about thick strings that can't be tied because of their thickness, though thin strings of the same length could be tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If they are thick and can't be tied, but if they were thin they could be tied, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises a new question about שמואל's 'enough to tie' test. What about strings that are long enough but too thick to tie?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is 'can it be tied?' A thick string of the same length might fail that test only because of its thickness, not because it is too short. So does the test really measure length, or does it measure whether this actual string can be tied?

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (raised a question)
Thick ones
Thin ones
Can be tied in a loop

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
Thick strings that cannot be tied,
but if they were thin they could be tied, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means thin strings of the same length.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: אַלִּימֵי דְּלָא מִיעַנְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks another question about שמואל's 'enough to tie' measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether thick strings that are long enough but too thick to tie still pass the 'enough to tie' test.

steps.title: All the more so: thick strings show the מצוה better
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא answers that thick strings are kosher all the more, because the מצוה is even more noticeable with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רבא said to רב אשי: All the more so, since their מצוה is more noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's question gets an answer: the thick strings are kosher, and even more so than thin ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test really measures length. If a thin string of this length is kosher, a thick string of the same length is surely kosher. Thick strings make the ציצית stand out even more as a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
Is noticeable, stands out
Their מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Cut-short ציצית strings stay kosher if enough remains to tie a loop. Whether that means all strings together or each alone is left as תיקו. Thickness doesn't hurt, since thick strings show the מצוה even more.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
All the more so, since their מצוה is more noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּמִינְּכַר מִצְוָתַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thick strings that would be tie-able if thin are kosher, all the more so, because the מצוה is more noticeable.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the opposite of רבי, meaning that תכלת and לבן do not depend on each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who argues with רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the תנא is that disagrees with רבי. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי held that you can't do the מצוה of ציצית without both the white strings and the תכלת strings. The גמרא now wants to know who holds the other side, that each kind of string works even without the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה
Disagrees, argues

phrases.english: And who is the תנא
who disagrees with רבי?
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who said the white and the תכלת strings depend on each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier discussion of רבי's opinion after the side questions about the length and thickness of the strings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name and source of the תנא who holds that תכלת and לבן do not depend on each other.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: without תכלת, put on white
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: רבי יוחנן בן נורי rules that if you have no תכלת, you still put on white strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יצחק says in the name of רבי נתן, who said in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן בן נורי: if a person has no תכלת, he puts on white strings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא who disagrees with רבי: רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The ruling reaches us through a chain of three sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says that without תכלת you still put on white strings. That shows the white strings work on their own, so the two kinds of string don't hold each other back. This is the exact opposite of רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The sky-blue strings of ציצית
The white strings of ציצית
Puts on, attaches

steps.whatToRemember: רבי says תכלת and לבן depend on each other. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says they do not: without תכלת, you still put on white.

phrases.english: It is this תנא,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נָתָן,
phrases.english: רבי יצחק says in the name of רבי נתן,
who said in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: who said in the name of רבי יוחנן בן נורי:
If he has no תכלת, he puts on white.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן בן נורי (through a chain of sages) holds that without תכלת one still puts on white, so the two do not depend on each other.

steps.title: רבא: a knot is needed after each set of windings
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that you must tie a knot after every set of windings in the ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from this that one must tie a knot after each and every set of windings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a new rule: a knot has to be tied after every set of windings, not just one knot at the end. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציצית strings are wound around in groups, called חוליות. רבא says each group needs its own knot to hold it in place. A single knot at the end is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from a source)
To tie a knot
One set of windings in the ציצית

phrases.english: רבא said: Learn from it
phrases.notes: He is learning this from the ruling of the sons of רבי חייא, which he quotes in the next lines.

phrases.english: that one must tie a knot
after each and every set of windings,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, how the ציצית must be tied, which רבא learns from the teaching of בני רבי חייא about cut-short strings (step 11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knot must be tied after every set of windings in the ציצית.

steps.title: Proof from cut-off strings being kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his rule from the sons of רבי חייא, who say cut-off strings are kosher. That only works if each set of windings has its own knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think a knot is not needed after each set, then look at what the sons of רבי חייא say: cut-off תכלת strings are kosher, and cut-off hyssop is kosher. But once the top came undone, the whole thing would come undone!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his rule. If there were only one knot, cutting the strings would make all the windings fall apart, so the cut strings could never be kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons of רבי חייא say ציצית strings that got cut short are still kosher. If only one knot held all the windings, losing the top would make the whole ציצית unravel and become worthless. Since cut strings are kosher, there must be a knot after each set that keeps the rest in place.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would think (sets up a wrong idea in order to reject it)
Cut-off leftovers of strings or branches
Hyssop, a plant used in purification rituals
Came undone, came loose

steps.whatToRemember: Cut-off ציצית strings are kosher only because each set of windings has its own knot. So, says רבא, you must tie a knot after every set.

phrases.english: For if you would think a knot is not needed,
then that which the sons of רבי חייא say:
cut-off תכלת strings are kosher
and cut-off hyssop is kosher,
once the top one came undone for him,
phrases.notes: 'The top one' means the top knot.

phrases.english: the whole thing would come undone for him!
phrases.notes: Then nothing kosher would be left, so how could cut strings be kosher? That's רבא's point.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לֹא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for רבא's rule in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a knot must be tied after each set of windings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sons of רבי חייא: cut-off תכלת strings and cut-off hyssop are kosher. That only makes sense if separate knots keep the windings from unraveling.
